reading_table.applied: G2a/G2b (golden/F0 feature + float model) match G1 sample-by-sample -> (a) rejected. G3 (quantized model + train feature) matches G1 sample-by-sample -> weight quantization/calibration intact. G2c/G4 (uint8 feature) collapse to top1=0 on BOTH float and quantized models -> the collapse enters exactly at the input uint8 quantization step. G2d/G4b (same z, corrected shift 36) match G1 sample-by-sample -> the collapse is fully and only explained by the 24-vs-36 shift bug.
reading_table.verdict: (b) quantization defect, sub-type: implementation bug in the golden/RTL QuantStub input quantization (4096x scale error), NOT an fbgemm calibration defect; secondary (c) fact: the float model itself discriminates weakly on these IRMAS samples (exact 1/5, piano all-correct) -> after the bug fix the board will show varied-but-mostly-wrong predictions on IRMAS-domain audio until a training-domain check or IRMAS retraining happens.

root_cause.primary: Input uint8 quantization scale bug: scripts/golden_pipeline.py quantize_int8 (line 554, round_half_even_shift(prod, QUANT_IN_FRAC_BITS=24)) and src/mel/standardize.v Beat Q (line 252-258, qprod_s48 = z_reg * INV_S_IN_S then q_shift = q_abs[47:24]) shift the product of z_q412 (Q4.12, 12 frac bits) and inv_s_in (Q8.24, 24 frac bits) by only 24 bits instead of 12 + 24 = 36 bits. The result is 4096x too large, so essentially every non-zero z bin saturates: measured 37.6..53.2 percent of bins == 0 and 46.7..62.2 percent of bins == 255 (~100 percent the feature is binarized) while the correctly shifted quantization saturates 0.0 %% on the same z.
root_cause.effect: The binarized feature destroys the spectrogram structure: BOTH the float checkpoint (G2c) and the deployed quantized model (G4, matching the bit-level golden and RTL of npu_probe_irmas_20261104.json) collapse to a constant top1=0 on all 8 IRMAS samples. RTL and golden stay bit-consistent with each other because they share the SAME buggy shift, so all previous golden-vs-RTL parity evidence remains valid as parity evidence, while both consume a broken input feature.
root_cause.class_table_note: reports/npu_probe_irmas_20261104.json reads top1=0 as 'piano' under an IRMAS-order table; the deployed model's label space is the Medley-solos-DB table (layer_contract.json classes), where index 0 is 'clarinet'. The constant-top1 symptom is unchanged.
root_cause.secondary: Domain shift: the float model (Medley-solos-DB training domain) only classifies piano (3/3 clips) and guitar_electric (nearest-class hit) correctly among these IRMAS clips; clarinet->piano, flute->piano, saxophone->distorted electric guitar, trumpet->female singer, violin->distorted electric guitar. Varied but mostly wrong -> IRMAS-vs-Medley domain mismatch is real but NOT the cause of the constant top1.

fix_path: RTL src/mel/standardize.v Beat Q: shift the s48 product by 36 bits instead of 24 (q_shift = q_abs[47:36], round-half-even threshold 2^35, rem width 36 bits; re-derive the wire widths accordingly). INV_S_IN / ZP_IN / the layer_contract quant_stub_input_contract and weights_image.bin are all unaffected - only the shift amount changes.
scripts/golden_pipeline.py quantize_int8: use frac = 12 + 24 = 36 (Z_Q412_FRAC_BITS + QUANT_IN_FRAC_BITS), keeping the round_half_even_shift call otherwise identical.

Regression guard: assert golden feat == frontend_variants.quantize_uint8(z_gold_float, s_in, zp_in) (already asserted per-sample in this run: fixed_matches_frontend_quant=true for 8/8 samples) and re-run the npu_probe IRMAS injection expecting the G4b column (top1 4/4/1/1/4/1/2/1) instead of the constant 0.

After the fix, re-check board behaviour on training-domain audio (Medley-solos-DB style clips): expect the G1/G3 predictions. For IRMAS-domain audio the fixed pipeline will still mis-classify most instruments (domain shift); full IRMAS accuracy needs training-domain re-validation or an IRMAS-domain retrain (note: no Medley class exists for acoustic guitar).

feature_domain_comparison.verdict: (a) rejected: train-domain, F0 and golden-domain features give sample-identical top1 on the float model (G1 == G2a == G2b); the acoustic parameters are identical (sr 44100 / n_fft 2048 / hop 512 / 64 slaney mels / fmax 22050 / power 2.0 / power_to_db ref=max top_db=80 / keep-tail 258 / per-sample z-norm). The only differences are numerical: integer (L+R+1)>>1 downmix vs librosa float mean, 132096-sample hardware window vs full 132299-sample file, fixed-point Q15/Q4.12 chain vs float chain - LSB-scale effects only (see feature_diffs), no top1 change.
feature_domain_comparison.quantization_input_convention: The deployed quantized model consumes the SAME float feature as the float model (deploy/inference_reference.py predict(): float (1,1,64,258) into the QuantStub forward); the uint8 domain (s_in=0.06266622245311737, zp_in=49) exists only inside the QuantStub / the NPU input image. fv.quantize_uint8 reproduces the fbgemm QuantStub semantics bit-exactly (run_compare S3); the golden/RTL shift bug is a re-implementation error of exactly this step.

conclusion.final: (b) quantization defect with a precisely localized implementation bug: the golden/RTL input uint8 quantization shifts z_q412 * inv_s_in by 24 instead of 36 bits (4096x scale error), binarizing the feature and collapsing every input to top1=0 (clarinet in the deployed Medley label space, misread as 'piano' in npu_probe under an IRMAS-order table). Feature-domain mismatch (a) is rejected; fbgemm weight quantization is intact (G3 == G1). Secondary (c): the float model is weak on IRMAS-domain clips (exact 1/5, piano 3/3) - fix the shift first, then re-evaluate on training-domain audio; full IRMAS accuracy needs domain re-validation or retraining.
conclusion.confidence: high - four-way closure: {float, quantized} model x {buggy, corrected} input quantization; the buggy uint8 collapses BOTH models, the corrected uint8 matches the float-feature result sample-by-sample, and the golden feature hash reproduces npu_probe 8/8 so the cited evidence and this run share the identical (broken) feature.
